answer: Each identity in an agent economy can be issued one walnut seed that generates a spiral of one-time canary codes, one code per claimed action, and a grove of verifier nodes tracks the next expected code. A verifier accepts an action only when its code matches that identity's next spiral step, and a repeated code is public proof of cloning, so both copies lose standing. An honest agent keeps one seed and spends one code per action, while an attacker running 1,000 clones must obtain 1,000 separate seeds, each through its own identity check, or see its clones expose themselves on a repeated code.
